title: Tool call schema hints and example-driven validation
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Background: As Redwood expands support for function/tool calling we need a pragmatic, developer-friendly schema format and validation runtime that balances strictness for safety with permissive migration for existing customers. Current issues: terse error messages, inconsistent coercion behavior between SDKs, and opaque telemetry that makes triage slow. Goal: define a compact JSON-dialect for tool parameter manifests, a validation strategy that produces actionable, example-driven errors, and a compatibility layer to accept legacy shapes during rollout.

Proposal summary:
- Introduce a lightweight schema DSL (compact-json-manifest or CJM) focused on common patterns (primitives, enums, nested objects, arrays) but intentionally limited to avoid full JSON Schema v2020 complexity. CJM will include: type, required, default, examples, coerce (bool), and deprecation aliasing for legacy keys.
- Runtime validation modes: strict (reject + error code), permissive-coerce (attempt coercion and log telemetry), and warn-only (accept but return structured warnings). Mode selection via per-route config + header override for debugging.
- Error taxonomy and payload: unify error responses into an action-centric shape {code, message, span, hint, example_fix}. Codes are short stable tokens (e.g., PARAM_MISSING, TYPE_MISMATCH, ENUM_VIOLATION, LEGACY_KEY_USED, COERCION_APPLIED). Each error includes a human hint and a minimal example showing the corrected parameter form.
- Example-driven errors: validators must attach an example_fix string with 1-2 lines showing corrected JSON for the minimal failing parameter set (helps quick remediation and can be surfaced in the Console).
- Compatibility layer: CJM supports "aliases" and a migration window. When a deprecated alias is used we emit LEGACY_KEY_USED and include the canonical key in hint and example_fix. We will default to permissive-coerce during a rollout window, then flip to strict.
- SDK/Server behavior: JS/py SDKs will apply client-side coercion in permissive modes to reduce round trips. Server-side validation is authoritative; telemetry tags include validation_mode, error_code, route, model, and sample hash (for privacy).
- Streaming and partial validation: For streaming tool calls we will validate syntactic contract at start (top-level required keys) and progressively validate nested chunks. Errors detected mid-stream should produce a streaming error frame with the same structured error payload.

Schema example (CJM snippet):
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "user_id": {"type": "string", "examples": ["u_12345"], "coerce": true},
    "limit": {"type": "integer", "default": 10, "coerce": true},
    "mode": {"type": "string", "enum": ["summary","full"], "examples": ["summary"]},
    "filters": {"type": "array", "items": {"type": "string"}},
    "sort": {"type": "string", "aliases": ["order_by"]}
  },
  "required": ["user_id"]
}

API error response example (HTTP 400):
{
  "error": {
    "code": "TYPE_MISMATCH",
    "message": "Parameter 'limit' expected integer but received \"5\" (string).",
    "span": "limit",
    "hint": "Send an integer or enable coerce mode to accept numeric strings.",
    "example_fix": "{ \"limit\": 5 }"
  }
}

Rollout plan:
1) Implement CJM parser + runtime validator behind a feature flag on staging (2 weeks).
2) Wire validator to Console and SDKs for warn-only mode and collect telemetry (1 week).
3) Run a 4-week permissive-coerce pilot with select customers (PM-led).
4) Flip to strict for new routes; provide migration tool (lint/transform) in Console to help customers update manifests.

Metrics to track: validation error rate, round trips due to validation failures, frequency of alias usage, coercion success rate, conversion time-to-fix (from error to corrected request).

Performance considerations: validation must be low-latency (target <0.5ms median at 95th p99 per request during validation path). Implement a compact compiled validator (ahead-of-time compiled checks) and cache CJM compiled forms per model-version-route.

Security & privacy: example_fix must not echo full user-provided PII. We will use a sample hash and only include sanitized values; include guardrails for long text.
acceptance_criteria: CJM parser accepts core constructs with unit tests covering coercion, aliasing, enums and nested arrays
Server-side validator returns structured error payloads with stable codes and example_fix
SDKs (JS/py) implement permissive-coerce client-side behavior behind a flag
Console surfaces errors and suggested fixes and includes a migration lint tool
Telemetry emits validation_mode, error_code, route, model, and anonymized sample hash
notes: Decision: favor a small DSL over full JSON Schema to reduce complexity and validate quickly
Trade-off: examples increase helpfulness but risk PII leakage; we'll sanitize before surface
Open question: how to represent complex nested union types in CJM without making DSL heavy
Integration note: streaming error frames reuse HTTP error codes but have a framed wire format for clients
